title: Gradient training fits overparameterized networks
description: Under suitable conditions, gradient training can bring large networks near zero training classification error.
bottom_line: Gradient training can drive large convolutional networks to zero or near-zero training error, even with random labels. Independent groups reproduce this on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Success depends on architecture, initialization and training recipe: smaller models and early stopping leave substantial training error. Batch normalization can speed training and shortcut connections can help deep networks train, but whether these benefits hold generally is contested. Fitting the training data well need not improve performance on unseen data.

claims.heading: Gradient training can fit large convolutional networks to near-zero training error
claims.summary: Several independent groups reproduce zero or near-zero training classification error with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels. Success depends on architecture, initialization and training recipe; smaller models, early stopping and some regularized recipes leave substantial training error.

claims.heading: Extra student neurons reduce getting stuck at poor solutions in shallow ReLU teacher–student networks
claims.summary: Several independent groups reproduce increasing trapping as equally wide teachers and students grow, and improved training with extra student width under modified procedures. These shallow teacher–student studies do not establish that extra width always eliminates trapping.

claims.heading: Depth can increase training error, and identity shortcuts can help
claims.summary: Independent studies support plain-network degradation and successful training with special initialization or Fixup in some settings. Broader claims of shortcut protection and reliable Fixup training are contested by reported convergence and replication failures.

claims.heading: Initialization controls training speed and trainable depth
claims.summary: Several independent groups reproduce the findings that initialization affects whether training succeeds and that, under some conditions, orthogonal weights train deep tanh networks faster than Gaussian weights. Orthogonal and Gaussian training dynamics become nearly equal in wide networks at small learning rates in the neural tangent kernel regime, where a linear approximation around the initial parameters describes training; the 10,000-layer CNN demonstration remains an original-study result.

claims.heading: Training can recover with learning rates too high for stable training at initialization
claims.summary: Independent groups reproduce recovery at learning rates above the limit for stable training at initialization with squared loss in small networks, and declining loss near the stability threshold in full-batch training. Staying near this threshold is not universal, and the complete recovery sequence remains unestablished in billion-parameter training.

claims.heading: Batch normalization can accelerate training, but its benefits depend on the setting
claims.summary: Several independent groups reproduce faster accuracy gains with batch normalization, but general claims of acceleration and higher learning-rate tolerance are contested. Fixup offers an alternative for residual networks, though its speed and stability also depend on the training setup.

reading_list.why: Establishes SGD fitting of true and random labels, with cropping and weight decay disabled for random labels.
Sigmoid VGG fitting depends on layer-skipping connections to the output and training duration, qualifying claims that any architecture fits.
Demonstrates frequent suboptimal local minima in realizable two-layer ReLU networks under expected squared-loss gradient descent and Xavier initialization.

known_gaps.summary: Unexplained convergence discrepancies, an omitted initialization comparison, unclear support for kernel qualifications and unresolved questions about factual accuracy limit confidence in the conclusions.
items: Reported global convergence at teacher width 17 and student width 19 differs between tables: 99.63% versus 77.50%. The reason for this discrepancy remains unexplained.

Initialization evidence remains incomplete without the comparison showing unsuccessful small-variance Gaussian initialization and successful Kaiming initialization in plain convolutional networks on MNIST and STL10. Its different training recipe limits direct comparison with other initialization results.
The qualification concerning neural tangent kernel descriptions needs explicit supporting results that readers can assess directly.
Several findings still have unresolved extraction or source discrepancies. Their factual reliability remains uncertain.
Evidence checks identified factual errors and incorrect interpretations. It remains unclear whether every affected conclusion was corrected or excluded.
Of 310 selected source checks, 305 were full reads; four remain partial and one has mismatched source text. Those five are not fully verified.
